tier_reason: mathbench-rs is public Criterion benchmark code (benches/ in bitshifter/mathbench-rs; the README tables come from commit 8e5467c, 2026-10-10) with compiler (Rust 1.99.0 b940084d7), flags (default profile.bench, documented) and CPU (AMD Ryzen 7 3800X, Linux) stated, and it runs glam against cgmath and nalgebra on the same rows. Every quoted number matches the scalar table.

corrections.claimed_speedup: mathbench scalar table, Ryzen 7 3800X, glam 0.34.1: matrix4 inverse 12.1455 ns vs cgmath 30.8124 ns and nalgebra 40.8410 ns (about 2.5x and 3.4x, derived from page data); matrix4 transpose 2.7248 ns vs 7.6718 ns and 7.7156 ns (about 2.8x, derived from page data); matrix4 determinant 4.3934 ns vs 7.1764 ns and 40.9609 ns; vector3 cross 1.0511 ns vs 1.5374 ns and 1.5364 ns; matrix4 mul matrix4 4.4589 ns vs 6.2970 ns and 4.7309 ns. Not faster everywhere: matrix4 mul vector4 x1 2.1002 ns vs nalgebra 1.9185 ns and cgmath 1.9625 ns; matrix2 mul matrix2 1.1531 ns vs cgmath 1.1030 ns; rotation3 mul vector3 x100 347.7 ns vs cgmath 307.8 ns; transform point2/vector2 x100 lose to euclid.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Rust 1.99.0 (b940084d7 2026-09-28), default cargo bench profile (no target-cpu, so SSE2 only on x86_64), command 'cargo bench --features scalar scalar'; tables produced at mathbench-rs commit 8e5467c (2026-10-10)
corrections.caveats: mathbench is written by glam's author, so the shootout is not independent. Default bench profile is used (no target-cpu=native), so SIMD benefit is limited to SSE2 width. The glam README itself gives no numbers and says wasm SIMD has not been benchmarked. Several rows are ties within 2.5% or small losses (matrix4 mul vector4 x1, matrix2 mul matrix2, rotation3 mul vector3, 2D transforms vs euclid). glam's matrix inverse does not check invertibility while cgmath and nalgebra return an Option, which accounts for part of the inverse gap (mathbench README says so). The README tables are stale relative to the code at HEAD: they were measured at commit 8e5467c (2026-10-10), before the 0.5.0 methodology change of 2026-10-11 (batched operations at sizes 16 and 1024 reported per element, glam Mat3A instead of Mat3 for matrix3 rows, Vec3A for vector3 length and rotation3 rows); later commits only renamed 'return self' rows to 'no-op baseline' and deleted wide rows by hand, so rerunning HEAD gives different row names and per-element numbers. Rust crate, not C++.

notes: Numbers verified row by row against the mathbench-rs README; tier A holds because code, compiler, flags and CPU are all public. Shortcomings to record: author-run shootout, SSE2-only default build, mixed results on several rows, unchecked inverse vs Option-returning baselines, and README tables that predate the 2026-10-11 benchmark methodology rewrite (reproduce at commit 8e5467c, not HEAD).

tier_reason: The harness (Makefile, drivers/, scripts/benchmark.sh) is public and the README states compilers, flags and CPUs, which would be A, but the baseline is deliberately de-optimized: scalar builds add -fno-tree-vectorize -fno-tree-loop-distribute-patterns (GCC) or -fno-vectorize -fno-slp-vectorize (icpx), so by analogy with the -O0 cap the win over a normal -O3 build is not shown; the RISC-V VL=4/VL=8 rows came from builds with temporary aliases that are not in the repo and no raw result CSVs are committed. Capped at C.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: GCC 14.1 (MareNostrum 5), icpx 2025.2, Homebrew GCC 15.2.0 (M1), conda-forge GCC 16.2 cross-compiler (RISC-V). Makefile: Linux -std=c++2b -O3 -march=native -mavx512f -mavx512vl -mavx512dq -mavx512bw -fno-math-errno -fno-trapping-math; macOS arm64 -std=c++2b -O3 -mcpu=apple-m1 -fno-math-errno -fno-trapping-math; RISC-V (README) -std=c++23 -O3 -march=rv64gcv_zvl256b -mrvv-vector-bits=zvl -static -fno-math-errno -fno-trapping-math. Scalar builds add -fno-tree-vectorize -fno-tree-loop-distribute-patterns (GCC) or -fno-vectorize -fno-slp-vectorize (icpx/clang). RISC-V VL=4 and VL=8 variants used separate builds with temporary SIMD aliases not in the repo.
corrections.caveats: Teaching study, not a reusable library; the SIMD side is libstdc++'s std::experimental::simd itself (std::simd is one of the category's listed baselines), so the entry measures std::simd code against scalar loops, not a library beating an incumbent. The baseline is deliberately de-vectorized scalar code, so the speedups say little about beating a normally compiled -O3 build; the exception is sum reduction and dot product, which GCC cannot auto-vectorize at -O3 without -ffast-math anyway, so those rows (5.37x and 1.78x on the Xeon with GCC) are the ones that would hold against a plain -O3 build. Element-wise add and memory-bound FMA are memory-traffic-limited (1.01x to 1.65x on x86 and RISC-V). The README itself notes that count_above on RISC-V contained no RVV instructions (gain is scalar unrolling), that icpx vectorizes softmax's exp loop through SVML, and that the large M1 clamp/count gains come from replacing branches with masks. x86 exercises 1-5 used three initial warm-ups instead of per-sample warm-ups and have not been refreshed. The RISC-V VL=4/VL=8 variants cannot be rebuilt from the repo (temporary aliases), and no result CSVs are committed (results/ is absent). M1 run had no core pinning. Repository history starts 2026-09-03, 0 stars, so results are unreviewed.

notes: All quoted speedups match the README tables. Downgraded A to C for a crippled baseline (auto-vectorization disabled in the scalar build), unreproducible RISC-V variants and missing raw results; the M1 build uses -mcpu=apple-m1, not -march=native. libstdc++ in baseline_stdlib is the SIMD implementation (std::experimental::simd), not the baseline; shortcomings to record: de-vectorized baseline, teaching study with 0 stars, stale x86 rows 1-5.

tier_reason: mathbench-rs wide benchmarks are public code (benches/ in bitshifter/mathbench-rs, tables from commit 8e5467c) with compiler (Rust 1.99.0), flags (RUSTFLAGS='-C target-feature=+avx2', default bench profile) and CPU (AMD Ryzen 7 3800X) stated, comparing ultraviolet wide types against glam doing the same work with one lane and against nalgebra's wide types. All quoted numbers match the wide table.

corrections.claimed_speedup: mathbench wide table, Ryzen 7 3800X, RUSTFLAGS -C target-feature=+avx2: ultraviolet_f32x8 vs glam_f32x1: euler 2d x80000 18.94 us vs 41.87 us (about 2.2x), euler 3d x80000 28.54 us vs 58.97 us (about 2.1x), ray-sphere intersection x80000 25.26 us vs 497.6 us (about 20x), matrix4 determinant x16 14.6545 ns vs 62.0342 ns (about 4.2x), vector3 normalize x16 7.3365 ns vs 35.2002 ns (about 4.8x), all ratios derived from page data. nalgebra_f32x8 is equal or within noise (euler 2d 18.57 us). Not faster everywhere: glam_f32x1 wins matrix4 transpose x16 (73.5089 ns vs 96.3356 ns for ultraviolet_f32x8) and ties matrix4 mul matrix4 x16 (163.5378 ns vs 167.0614 ns); at x256 most rows are ties (matrix2 mul matrix2 x256 688.9 ns vs 678.7 ns, transform point2 x256 691.8 ns vs 683.6 ns).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Rust 1.99.0 (b940084d7 2026-09-28), RUSTFLAGS='-C target-feature=+avx2' cargo bench --features wide wide; ultraviolet 0.10.0; tables produced at mathbench-rs commit 8e5467c (2026-10-10)
corrections.caveats: The comparison is against glam's one-lane scalar type doing the same amount of work, so the large ratios mostly measure SoA batching, not a better library; nalgebra's f32x8 types match ultraviolet, and glam_f32x1 still wins matrix4 transpose x16 and ties matrix4 mul matrix4 x16, while ultraviolet_f32x4 is slower than glam on matrix2 and matrix3 transpose x16. Gains shrink to ties at x256 sizes. In mathbench's scalar table ultraviolet wins outright only the matrix2 and matrix3 transpose rows. The ray-sphere ratio (about 20x for 4-8 lanes) suggests the glam_f32x1 path is unusually slow on that row: 497.6 us for x80000 is about 4.7x glam's own scalar-table rate of 13.37 us per x10000 (derived from page data). mathbench is written by glam's author. The tables predate mathbench 0.5.0 (2026-10-11 rewrite to batched per-element throughput at sizes 16 and 1024; wide 'return self' rows were deleted by hand), so HEAD does not reproduce the exact rows. The repository has moved to github.com/fu5ha/ultraviolet (Cargo.toml and crates.io still name termhn). No license text file exists in the repo (LICENSE, LICENSE-MIT, LICENSE-APACHE, LICENSE-ZLIB all 404); the MIT OR Apache-2.0 OR Zlib expression is only in Cargo.toml and crates.io metadata. HEAD is 0.11.0 (breaking migration to wide 1.7, unreleased; crates.io max is 0.10.0 from 2025-04-26); the benchmark used 0.10.0. Rust crate, not C++.

notes: Numbers verified against the mathbench-rs wide table; tier A stays. Repo moved to fu5ha/ultraviolet: consider a repo_url override. Shortcomings to record: wins mostly measure SoA batching vs one-lane glam, ties with nalgebra wide, glam wins matrix4 transpose x16, anomalous glam ray-sphere row, author-run shootout with tables predating the 0.5.0 methodology, license declared only in Cargo.toml.
